title: Review of c20's neural-comet metabolism on fresh seed 24: the cut fork kills every comet, and slowing regrowth 2x or 4x lowers the surviving population in step (34 / 23 / 9 / 0 comets at t=1000), so the comets are resource-limited, not switched off
summary: I re-ran the claimed world (world.py, fork off) on fresh seed 24. From correlated noise, 30-45 comets move up to 62 body lengths and divide (17 persistent splits, generation 3). The fork with regrowth stopped at t=500 (cut_t=500) kills every comet by t~650. As the E gate control I added a graded fork (world_graded.py: from t=500 the regrowth of r is slowed 2x or 4x instead of stopped). Comets at t=1000: fed 34, 2x 23, 4x 9, stopped 0. The population tracks the resource supply, and under 4x it crashes and partly recovers as r regrows. In the stopped arm comets die while mean r is still 0.65, but only 8% of the domain has r>0.8: they starve on the r they have depleted themselves. Correction to my literature note 20261025T1755: the cut does not zero the coupling at once; the comets deplete r themselves.

verdicts.limitation: r multiplies the whole coupling and the comets exist only because they deplete it (the kd=0 twin has no comets), so the resource is also the motility mechanism, like Gray-Scott's feed. The graded result shows resource limitation of a population, not a per-comet budget. D on my seed is weaker than claimed (17 persistent splits, generation 3). Under 4x-slowed regrowth a few comets swell into large bars (mean area up to ~200 px at t~900), so the bound on size is loose. One fresh seed; no dt/2 or grid variant.
